method: Multi-institution review incl. WHO (Rossert HQ colleagues, Uganda/Tanzania/Rwanda)
finding: ART-R has emerged in multiple East African countries and is now a priority; recommended expansion of genomic surveillance, clinical efficacy trials, ex-vivo susceptibility testing, policy adaptation
limitations: Review / recommendation piece, no new primary data

method: 173 P. falciparum-positive children, Mwanza, Tanzania (2016-2022), 143 Pfk13 sequenced
finding: 7.0% non-synonymous Pfk13 mutations incl. WHO-validated R561H (2 patients, 2022); pfmdr1 N86 invariable; mean MOI 1.5; suggests emerging lumefantrine tolerance

method: Systematic review + meta-analysis of 24 studies (2014-2024), East Africa
finding: Pooled non-synonymous PfKelch13 prevalence 5.0% (Cl 3.0-7.0%); R561H and A675V most common; mutations associated with higher risk of treatment failure (log OR -2.06)
Five validated pfk13 ART-R markers in Africa: R561H (Rwanda, Tanzania), M476I (Tanzania), C580Y (Ghana), F446I (Mali), P553L (Angola); distribution central to East Africa

method: Symptomatic malaria patients at primary centres, central Ethiopia, 2023 (220 isolates)
finding: Validated ART-R marker pfk13 R622I in ~2/174 (1.1%); pfmdr1 pattern consistent with reduced lumen sensitivity; high HRP2/3-deletion prevalence (HRP2 del 24%, HRP3 del 79%, dual 22.7%)

method: Aggregation of 112,933 P. falciparum samples (1980-2023), review
finding: ART-R in Africa follows the Southeast Asia pattern 10-15 years earlier; kelch13 data aggregated into a single surveillance resource with focus on East Africa

method: Review of artemisinin-based combination therapy resistance (Pfk13, partner drugs)
finding: ART resistance is mediated by kelch13; ACTs remain effective but partner-drug vulnerabilities and regional spread of markers demand continual monitoring
